newsitem.title: USA: "Air Force One" takes off at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Air Force One" takes off at U.S. box office.

text.p: "Air Force One," a hijack thriller starring Harrison Ford as the president of the United States, soared to the top of the box office in its opening weekend, according to studio estimates released on Sunday.

The film earned about $37.1 million, and was followed by "George of the Jungle" with $13.2 million and defending box office champ "Men in Black" with $12.6 million. The only other new entry in the top 10 was the children's film "Good Burger," which opened in fifth with $7.3 million.
"Air Force One" smashed several records along the way, as well as earning warm praise from the real president, Bill Clinton, who told reporters over the weekend that it was a "very good movie."

But he pointed out that the film took some liberties with the facts: the action takes place aboard the president's Boeing 747, and the filmmakers equipped it with an escape pod and a back door, neither of which exist, Clinton said. One other key difference was that Ford earned a reported $20 million, exactly 10 times Clinton's salary.

A spokesman for Columbia Pictures, which released the movie, said "Air Force One" is Ford's biggest opener, breaking the benchmark of $31.5 million established by the "Star Wars" re-release earlier this year. It's also the biggest opening for an "R"-rated movie, surpassing the $36.3 million opening in November 1994 of "Interview with the Vampire."
Columbia is a unit of Sony Corp..
"George of the Jungle" held steady at second in its second weekend, and has now earned $48.1 million. The family comedy is released by Walt Disney Co..
Columbia's "Men in Black," which had ruled the box office for the past three weekends, slipped two places to third. The total for the alien sleuth comedy stands at $194.3 million.
Fourth place went to "Contact," with $9.5 million, which takes its three-week total to $64.8 million. The Jodie Foster sci-fi picture is released by Warner Bros., a unit of Time Warner Inc..
